lead: Quiet day: the strongest usable material is about changing how engineers work with coding agents, not a new model or supervisory requirement. Stanford’s CS146S course and Monaco’s engineering team both emphasise repository context, human review and learning to assess changes rather than accepting one-shot output. The separate Git-forge report describes repeated evaluation and explicit merge gates, but it is a secondary account of a product announcement and needs verification before an adoption decision. For your own engineering pilots, test whether these practices improve accepted changes and review quality without weakening existing controls.

items.title: How Stanford Teaches AI-Native Engineering — Mihail Eric, Monaco
items.summary: Stanford’s CS146S course now asks students to contribute to open-source projects, where maintainers review their patches; the interview says many prior exercises had become one-prompt tasks. Monaco’s AI engineering team uses Devin for code review and built its own agent workspaces for running the product, reproducing failures and testing patches; the article states no measured productivity result.
items.so_what: Trial maintainer-style review and isolated agent workspaces in a bounded coding-agent pilot, measuring accepted changes, rework and defects rather than counting generated code.

items.title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
items.summary: InfoQ reports that Entire’s forge runs review agents in cloud sandboxes and updates evaluation scores on each push, with repository-level gates requiring findings to be resolved or closed before merge. The report describes configurable checks for code quality, security and human-review needs, plus persistent repository and session context; pricing, availability regions and independently measured outcomes are not stated.
items.so_what: Benchmark its repeated-evaluation and merge-gate pattern against your current CI and code-review controls, but verify the implementation and security boundary before adopting a new forge.
